decision: Retain the tested Cherrypharm Montmorency cherry–apple blend as a controlled acute-function research reserve. Preserve the 2006 strength positive and separately identified 2019 concentrate counterevidence. No generic-cherry, pooled efficacy, structural muscle-protection, BUBR1-restoration or MVA-superiority claim.
identity_boundary: One exact proprietary cherry–apple blend appraisal. CherryActive concentrate and POM Wonderful are separate comparison preparations, not aliases or additional positive nominations. Current retail equivalence and approved-drug eligibility remain unestablished.

citation.title: Efficacy of a tart cherry juice blend in preventing the symptoms of muscle damage

studies.decision: Retain a preparation-specific acute muscle-function protection signal for independent review; no chronic MVA efficacy, BUBR1-restoration or clinical-superiority claim.

preparation.name: Cherrypharm proprietary Montmorency tart-cherry and apple juice blend
preparation.plant_material: Frozen tart cultivar Montmorency cherries; freshly prepared juice, not concentrate
preparation.apple: Commercially available apple juice; proprietary undisclosed ratio
preparation.processing: Heated to 85 C, hot packed in 12 oz glass bottles with three-minute hold, water-bath cooled

per_bottle_reported.phenolics_basis: Gallic acid equivalents, Singleton and Rossi method

preparation.source_exposure: 12 fl oz twice daily for eight days, eccentric challenge on fourth supplementation day; trial history only
preparation.comparator: Unsweetened black-cherry Kool-Aid in water at approximately 2 g/L; sugar added to 13 Brix; same pasteurization/bottling
preparation.matching_limit: Soluble solids matched; an analytical calorie comparison and apple-only comparator not reported
identity_limits: No separation of cherry and apple effects

design.reported: Randomized placebo-controlled crossover with randomized arm and treatment order
design.blinding: Participant/assessor masking not described; do not assign double-blind from this main
design.population: Men, mean age 22 years SD 4; no elbow pain, recent upper-extremity strength training or elbow/shoulder injury history

withdrawals.reason: Left school at semester end before completing protocol

design.analysis: Completers; no intention-to-treat result, imputation or missing-sequence sensitivity supplied
design.challenge: Two sets of 20 maximal eccentric elbow-flexion contractions, three-minute set rest, about three seconds/contraction and 12 seconds between contractions
design.period_timing: Second baseline two weeks after initial baseline, six days after end of first trial; opposite arm used
design.washout_limit: Not a two-week treatment-free washout; no verified pharmacological washout
design.crossover_limit: Contralateral muscle avoids same-local-muscle repeat exposure but does not demonstrate absence of cross-limb, systemic, learning or period effects; formal treatment-by-period/sequence model unreported
design.baseline_timing: Before drink supply at beginning of each period; described as four days before challenge
design.adherence: Quantitative drink adherence and achieved eccentric workloads not supplied
design.restrictions: No upper-extremity exercise, anti-inflammatory/pain-relieving drugs or other damage treatments; lower-body activity not prohibited

measurement.strength: Force-transducer peak voluntary isometric elbow-flexion force in Newtons; mean of two contractions at each of 130,90,30-degree flexion angles
measurement.published_strength_scale: Percent of period-specific baseline, averaged across angles
measurement.inference_limit: A percent-of-baseline force difference is functional evidence but not a published absolute Newton treatment effect or durable strength gain
measurement.pain: Subjective 0–10 discomfort with active movements/daily activities
measurement.tenderness: Threshold applied force at distal biceps site, difference from baseline

sequence_sensitivity.timing: Discussion reports reanalysis; not an independent prospective endpoint
sequence_sensitivity.interpretation: Strength result argues against a simple second-period-only protective explanation, but does not resolve all carryover/period mechanisms or missing sequences

statistics.sample_size: Planned 16, 80% power at p<.05 for stated 14% difference in strength loss; detectable pain/tenderness/motion differences also provided
statistics.planned_primary: Strength anchors sample size; no independently verified prospective single-primary hierarchy
statistics.model: Treatment-by-time repeated-measures ANOVA; strength also assesses angle interactions
statistics.multiplicity: Bonferroni correction explicitly reported for treatment-versus-placebo pairwise comparisons; across-endpoint family adjustment not reported
statistics.registry: No identifier or recruitment dates in main; exact-title ClinicalTrials.gov query yielded zero; no exhaustive registration-absence claim

mechanism.hypothesis: Antioxidant/anti-inflammatory attenuation of secondary response to exercise damage

safety.withdrawal_cause: Reported departure from school, not assigned a treatment adverse-event cause

transparency.conflict: Paper discloses each author holds 2.5% equity in Cherrypharm Inc
transparency.PubMed_comment: CommentIn PMID 17092438; not read here and not a correction
transparency.correction_retraction_notice: None in inspected PubMed/Crossref fields; bounded check

competitiveness.retained: Direct controlled acute strength-protection observation in healthy exercisers
not_established: Clinical superiority or inferiority versus niacin/apitegromab
competitiveness.advancement_standard: Relevant-model useful output, justified exposure, renewable reserve and chromosome fidelity; BUBR1 mediation additionally needed only if claiming restoration

studies.reading_depth: Complete scientific main from lawful PMC HTML, all four native outcome figures/captions; no results tables or linked supplement in main. PDF routes failed; no PDF reading credit.

citation.title: No Effect of Tart Cherry Juice or Pomegranate Juice on Recovery from Exercise-Induced Muscle Damage in Non-Resistance Trained Men

studies.decision: Preparation-specific randomized functional counterevidence: no statistically detectable recovery benefit, but not an equivalence test or exact-product refutation of the 2006 Cherrypharm cherry–apple blend. No repository addition or nomination change authorized by this packet.

preparation.active: CherryActive Ltd., Hanworth, UK tart-cherry concentrate

per_serving.energy_adjustment: Maltodextrin from My Protein added to match 250 mL POM Wonderful. Exact grams/calories not supplied.

preparation.cultivar_and_lot: Intervention Methods do not explicitly identify cultivar, batch or source-fruit composition; do not certify Montmorency lot identity from the brand alone.
preparation.apple: No apple ingredient or blending ratio supplied for the tested concentrate. Do not assign the 2006 cherry–apple preparation to this trial.
preparation.control: Science in Sport Energy Go blackcurrant-flavored maltodextrin sports drink, prepared to match energy of both active drinks.
preparation.other_active_arm: 250 mL undiluted POM Wonderful pomegranate juice. This arm is context from the same trial, not a separate preparation appraisal or independent cohort.
preparation.source_schedule: One 250 mL serving in the morning and one in the evening for 9 days; an extra 250 mL immediately after the day-5 exercise challenge. Trial description only.
preparation.abstract_ambiguity: Abstract wording 2 × 250 mL ... twice daily is clarified by Methods as two routine daily servings, not four.
preparation.handling: Fresh drinks prepared/delivered every two days, brown bottles to mask color from investigators; participants instructed to refrigerate.

characterization.assays: Three bottles per juice analyzed in triplicate; Folin–Ciocalteu phenolics as gallic-acid equivalents, pH differential monomeric anthocyanins as cyanidin-3-glucoside equivalents.
characterization.limits: No systemic exposure, identified active-compound dose, tissue uptake or composition-mediated efficacy test.
characterization.dispersion_type: The original chemical-assay Results do not identify the reported ± quantities as SD or SEM. Values are retained without assigning a dispersion type.

design.type: Randomized, reported double-blind, energy-matched placebo-controlled parallel trial with three arms
design.population: Non-resistance-trained men; eligibility age 18–65, nonsmoking, injury-free, no upper-body strength training for 3 months, no current anti-inflammatories or antioxidant supplements.
design.randomization: Computerized random block order, block sizes 3 and 6, generated by researcher outside participant recruitment.
design.concealment: No additional explicit allocation-concealment procedure described.
design.masking: Separate technician prepared drinks in brown bottles, outside data collection; participants told different fruit-flavored drinks were under investigation and unaware which was placebo. No masking-success assessment reported.
design.sequence_carryover: Not applicable to this parallel trial. No participant crosses between treatments; avoids treatment-period and cross-limb crossover carryover.
design.familiarization: Minimal-effort practice intended to avoid unintentional damage or repeated-bout protection; absence of any adaptation not experimentally established.
design.challenge: Day 5: 50 maximal eccentric nondominant elbow-flexor contractions, 5 sets of 10, forced extension 90° to 180° at 60°/s, 12-second intervals and 2-minute interset rest.
design.baseline: Day-5 pre-exercise measurement after four supplementation days and morning drink. Not a pre-supplement strength baseline.
design.cointerventions: Standardized immediate post-exercise meal providing 0.3 g protein/kg body weight; chicken or cheese option. Other foods/drinks except water avoided for 3 hours. Strenuous exercise, other recovery measures, supplements and polyphenol-rich foods discouraged.
design.adherence: All drinks reportedly consumed; empty bottles counted. Two participants consumed both daily servings in the evening on one day. Background polyphenol foods persisted; diary means did not differ detectably (P=.44).

strength.basis: Figure 2 caption; omnibus residual group df 30 also consistent with 33 analyzed.

missing_observations: One placebo participant missed 72-hour measurements owing to illness.
One pomegranate CK value at 48 hours missing for technical reasons.
One cherry and one pomegranate MIVC value at 72 hours missing for technical reasons.
denominators_and_missingness.handling: All 36 trial completers are not the strength-analysis denominator. No imputation method supplied; figure captions give complete-series n rather than all randomized n.

hyper_responders.definition: Post-exercise CK >2000 U/L at any time point
hyper_responders.exploratory_analysis: Excluded separately; endpoint-specific remaining n and overlap with missing observations not supplied, so do not assume every analysis is 10 per arm.

outcome_hierarchy.prespecified_primary: Not independently verified; main does not specify a single primary outcome or registration ID.
outcome_hierarchy.power: No sample-size calculation supplied. Discussion acknowledges that small parallel groups may miss small/moderate effects.
outcome_hierarchy.registry: Bounded ClinicalTrials.gov tart cherry pomegranate query returned zero records; an initial exact-title request returned HTTP 400. Registration elsewhere or under different terms remains unknown.
outcome_hierarchy.protocol_and_raw_data: No public protocol, SAP, supplement or participant dataset obtained; no scientific supplement linked in retained main.
outcome_hierarchy.endurance: No endurance-performance test or chronic muscle-strength outcome.

measurement.strength: Biodex dynamometer, mean of five 3-second maximal voluntary isometric elbow-flexion contractions at 90°, 10-second rests.
measurement.strength_effect_scale: Percent of day-5 pre-exercise strength; no absolute force treatment contrast supplied.
measurement.baseline_unit_issue: Table 1 labels baseline strength N·cm⁻² without explaining area normalization; retain ambiguity, do not silently correct or treat as demonstrated specific force.
measurement.soreness: 100-mm VAS after two biceps curls with a 1-kg dumbbell.
measurement.ROM: Maximal elbow flexion and extension measured by goniometer, total range calculated; efficacy as percent of pre-exercise.
measurement.CK: Finger-prick whole-blood CK; capillary assay, dilution for values above assay range.
measurement.dispersion: Native figures mean ± SEM; baseline characteristics use mean ± SD or median/IQR as specified.

strength.interpretation: Omnibus three-group tests, not pairwise cherry-versus-placebo tests. Arithmetic mean-loss difference is descriptive, not a demonstrated benefit.

time_effect.posthoc: Bonferroni differences from pre-exercise through 72 hours; not at 96 hours (P=.08).

ROM.reporting_discrepancy: Abstract locates maximum decrease at 72 hours and time P=.001; Results says 48 hours and P<.001 and prints malformed-looking F degrees of freedom. No silent reconciliation; treatment null tests retained.

CK.reporting_note: Abstract gives maximum increase 1385 U/L; Results describes peak 1383 U/L. No digitized/recomputed estimate or correction supplied.

hyper_responder_exclusion.role: Exploratory sensitivity within the same trial, not independent replication or primary analysis.

statistics.main_model: Mixed ANOVA: time within participant, treatment between participant. Strength and ROM normalized to baseline.
statistics.sphericity: Greenhouse–Geisser correction when Mauchly test failed.
statistics.multiplicity: Bonferroni post-hoc tests for significant time effects; no reported family-wide correction across four outcomes.
statistics.null_limit: Small samples, no equivalence/noninferiority design and no pairwise treatment CIs mean nonsignificance cannot establish zero effect.
statistics.positive_evidence_retained: A clear exercise-induced force decrement validates that recovery could be observed; descriptive cherry strength trajectory is numerically favorable but not statistically established. Earlier blend benefit is preserved in its own packet.

safety.missed_visit: One placebo participant ill at 72 hours; no treatment attribution supplied.
safety.CK_hyper_response: Two per arm after deliberate damage; this is an exercise-response subgroup, not established supplement toxicity.
safety.transfer: No long-term, pediatric, cancer or MVA safety claim supported.

funding.present_study: Sheffield Hallam University and University of Sheffield
funding.disclosure: Anthony Lynn received a Cherry Marketing Institute grant for a separate gout study; Kirstie Lamb was working on that study. Other authors declare no conflicts.
funding.limit: Do not relabel the present university-funded trial as industry-funded based only on the separate disclosed grant. Product donation or further sponsor role not stated.

context_bindings.scope: Read-only context from frozen 2006 qualification, not fresh primary-paper reading
Read-only context from frozen 2006 qualification, not fresh primary-paper reading

comparison_to_connolly2006.shared_relevance: Healthy untrained men, eccentric elbow-flexor injury challenge and measured voluntary isometric recovery through 96 hours. Functional counterevidence, not merely biomarker nulls.
comparison_to_connolly2006.preparation_difference: CherryActive concentrate plus water/maltodextrin versus Cherrypharm fresh-from-frozen Montmorency cherry–apple blend with proprietary apple ratio.
comparison_to_connolly2006.composition_difference: 2019 serving measured 294.7 mg phenolics/7.7 mg monomeric anthocyanins; 2006 bottle reported at least 600/40 mg in equivalent assay units. Dose/composition causality not established.
comparison_to_connolly2006.design_difference: 2019 parallel 12 randomized per arm, strength 11 per arm, versus 2006 imbalanced completer crossover 14 with period/cross-limb concerns.
comparison_to_connolly2006.challenge_difference: 50 versus 40 eccentric contractions; different strength angles/measurement protocols, supplementation/baseline timing and standardized post-exercise meal.
comparison_to_connolly2006.interpretation: Qualifies generic product/category transfer; does not prove the exact 2006 blend ineffective. Neither paper supplies a head-to-head clinical comparison against niacin/apitegromab.

competitiveness.supports: Keep preparation-specific recovery evidence and counterevidence together, with product chemistry and analysis scope.
limits: No BUB1B/BUBR1 assay or restoration mechanism
No evidence sufficient to displace disease-relevant provisional nominees
No class-wide cherry, polyphenol or pomegranate efficacy/toxicity conclusion
competitiveness.fairness: BUBR1 restoration is not required to acknowledge measured functional protection/recovery. Model relevance and exposure/long-term transfer remain separate limitations.

notices_and_access.notice_check: No correction/retraction relations in current retained PubMed XML or Crossref metadata. Bounded check, not universal absence.
notices_and_access.main: Complete scientific main and two tables read from lawful official Europe PMC XML/PMC HTML.
notices_and_access.native: All five native figures and captions visually inspected from official Europe PMC assets.
notices_and_access.supplement: supplementaryFiles ZIP contained only five JPG figures and GIF thumbnails; no separate scientific supplement linked in main.
notices_and_access.pdf: Publisher PDF HTTP 403; no PDF reading credit or bypass.

2019_dispersion.reason: Independent primary reading did not find SD/SEM defined for these chemical-assay ± values; source and participant-table dispersion labels must not be conflated.

integration_precision_corrections.2006_control: Listed Kool-Aid ingredients include ascorbic acid, quantity unreported. It is a flavored soluble-solids-matched control, not proven inert, plain sugar water or analytically calorie-matched.
integration_precision_corrections.baseline_estimands: The 2006 baseline precedes supplementation, without a reported immediate pre-exercise re-baseline; 2019 normalizes to day-five pre-exercise values after four supplementation days and the morning drink. Percentage estimands differ.
integration_precision_corrections.functional_not_structural: The measured post-challenge strength contrast is real functional evidence. It does not distinguish prechallenge strengthening, altered voluntary activation, less damage or faster recovery.
integration_precision_corrections.2019_analysis_set: Endpoint counts and degrees of freedom are consistent with excluding incomplete series, but that analysis rule is inferred rather than explicitly reported; no imputation is stated.

identity.title: Dietary factors as novel therapies for muscle pain
identity.author: Roland Staud
identity.indexing: Comment on PMID 16790484, not an indexed correction or retraction
identity.date_discrepancy: PubMed gives December 2006; publisher/Crossref give November 2006. No outcome inference depends on resolving this bibliographic difference.

full_text.publisher_result: Subscription preview with references and metadata; scientific commentary body absent. Standard PDF endpoint returned the same HTML preview and failed the PDF signature check.
full_text.europepmc_result: No PMC/Europe PMC full text, no PDF; subscription-required DOI link.
full_text.lawful_copy_search: Exact title/DOI and author-institution checks found no usable primary or institutional full text; bounded, not exhaustive.

author_response.checked: PubMed CommentOn/CommentIn relations for commentary and parent; Crossref relation/update metadata; visible publisher preview links; exact DOI reply/response search.
author_response.access_limit: Parent BMJ responses endpoint returned HTTP 403. No assertion that a response never existed.

scientific_delta.masking: No change justified by this retrieval. Existing source-qualified masking uncertainty stays in place. Do not attribute a masking criticism or defense to Staud.
scientific_delta.crossover: No change justified. Retain prior limits on period/carryover and the small blend-first subgroup countercheck without attributing either to Staud.
scientific_delta.outcome_inference: No new effect estimate, endpoint interpretation or strength/pain claim obtained. The existing direct functional positive remains; unread commentary cannot strengthen or nullify it.
scientific_delta.proprietary_blend: No newly read composition disclosure. Preserve the exact cherry–apple blend identity and undisclosed ratio; do not generalize to isolated cherry constituents or other preparations.
scientific_delta.commentary_opinion: Unknown because body unavailable. No opinion has been substituted for trial data.

integration_recommendation.reason: The citation relationship and remaining source-access gap are verified; scientific content and any response are unreviewed. This retrieval neither disqualifies the existing primary-trial qualification nor supplies positive or negative efficacy credit.
integration_recommendation.suggested_sentence: A later commentary by Staud (PMID 17092438) is indexed on the Connolly trial, but lawful retrieval yielded only subscription-preview metadata and references; its scientific content and any author response remain unreviewed. No efficacy inference or new study credit is assigned.

competitiveness.positive_credit: The 2006 crossover reports less measured strength loss with the blend, including corrected daily treatment comparisons. The blend-first sensitivity strengthens the functional signal without creating an independent cohort.
competitiveness.counterevidence_credit: The 2019 parallel concentrate study has a measurable exercise-induced strength deficit and no detected treatment recovery advantage. Its omnibus tests and absent pairwise CIs do not establish equivalence or refute a different product.
competitiveness.comparison_limits: Preparation/composition, design, baseline timing, challenge intensity, cointerventions, missingness and short healthy-exercise settings prevent an interchangeable-product or clinical-potency ranking. No pooled estimate is computed.
competitiveness.nominees: Niacin/restoration and apitegromab/compensation remain provisional. Missing MVA rescue cannot be demanded uniquely of this challenger, but neither study demonstrates superiority over those different clinical/mechanistic comparisons.
competitiveness.next: Identify reproducible preparation or relevant metabolites and justified measured exposure; test useful absolute muscle output, renewable reserve and chromosome fidelity in appropriate affected/corrected models. Functional BUBR1 mediation is additional only for restoration claims.

root_reading.2006: Complete source qualification and independent review; original preparation, comparator, baseline/sequence, strength Results and Discussion passages; native strength Figure 1. Not a second complete root scientific-main read.
root_reading.2019: Complete source qualification and independent review; selected original Methods, missingness, strength Results, composition and Discussion passages; native strength Figure 2. Not all native figures or the complete main independently re-read by root.
root_reading.independent: Both full scientific mains, all nine native figures and both 2019 native HTML tables read independently; separate subordinate 2019 check. Exact scopes retained in frozen packets.
root_reading.commentary: Root read the completed source-limit finding. Commentary scientific body and any associated response remain unreviewed; no opinion inferred from metadata.
